title: Grateful Dead Live at The Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-26
source: S:MR> DATx5> CD, including patches (see info file for specifics

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the May 26 1972 London show, highlighted by a smoking Truckin’→The Other One→Morning Dew sequence and stellar performances throughout.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers an almost flawless soundboard mix that lets every instrument shine—from Keith’s front‑line piano to Pigpen’s organ—while the band roars at peak energy. The first set rolls through 19 songs with tight transitions, and the second set erupts into a legendary Truckin’/Other One/Morning Dew suite plus standout renditions of Cumberland Blues, Dire Wolf, Playing in the Band and Two Souls in Communion. Minor tuning hiccups and a slightly rough “He’s Gone” are the only blemishes on an otherwise superb night.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show and recording five stars, praising both performance and audio quality; only a handful note minor issues, leading to an average rating near 5 with high confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with superb stereo imaging; occasional hiss and a slight warble on “He’s Gone”; minor tuning slips between first‑set songs but overall the sound is pristine.

standout_songs: Truckin' > The Other One > Morning Dew
China Cat > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A marathon 19‑song first set that feels like a second set, with tight segues (NFA > GDTRFB > NFA) and an explosive second‑set suite: Truckin' → The Other One → Drums → The Other One → Morning Dew → The Other One → Sing Me Back Home.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is described as perfect and “off the wall” on the jams; his vocals on ‘He’s Gone’ and especially the emotional delivery of ‘Morning Dew’ receive high praise.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work is called “bombs” and prominently featured in the mix, with notable vocal contributions on ‘He’s Gone’; several reviewers highlight his spots during jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and soloing are praised, particularly on Jack Straw and during interplay with Garcia in the extended jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is lauded for front‑line piano work, aggressive comping during the Second Set jams, and his organ/piano balance with Pigpen; his playing is called “extraordinary” and a key driver of the jam energy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming gets commendation for a solid drum solo and tight support throughout the percussion‑driven sections, especially in the long Other One suite.
